messages.subject: Re: Sign reversal in standardised estimates in latent model
messages.subject_clean: Sign reversal in standardised estimates in latent model
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ellen,
I'm not sure what you are viewing as the issue. Your results indicate that loneliness is primarily associated with F1 and, after controlling for mutual relations between F1, F2, and F3, there is not much of an association between loneliness and F2 or F3.... Given that your depression and anxiety phenotypes load on F1 this doesn't seem too surprising. I'm not sure I would call a drop from a moderate positive correlation to a slightly negative regression coefficient a concerning sign reversal. We see it here too (minute 19) in a simpler model: https://youtu.be/ECwQS5UD3YM?t=1144
It is also something that is common in OLS regression...

--
Elliot M. Tucker-Drob, Ph.D.
Professor
Department of Psychology
Faculty Research Associate
Population Research Center
The University of Texas at Austin
108 E. Dean Keeton Stop A8000
Austin, TX 78712-0187
tucke...@utexas.edu
www.lifespanlab.com <http://www.lifespanlab.com/>

On Wed, Dec 2, 2020 at 8:13 AM Ellen Martin <martin.e...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Attachment didn't seem to work so here it is again.
>
> On Wednesday, 2 December 2020 at 14:02:47 UTC Ellen Martin wrote:
> > Hello,
> >
> > I am attempting to run a latent factor model in which the latent factors are associated with another observed factor LONELINESS.
> >
> > F1 =~ NA*ADHD + ANX + MDD + PTSD + ASD
> > F2 =~ NA*BIP + SCZ + OCD
> > F3 =~ NA*ALC6UNITS + COCA + SMK + CAN
> >
> > F1~~F2+F3
> > F2~~F3
> >
> > LONELINESS ~ F1 + F2 + F3
> >
> > The CFA model (excluding regression between LONELINESS and the three latent factors) converged without any apparent issues. However, when I included loneliness, there were sign reversals between LONELINESS and F2 and LONELINESS and F3, perhaps due to multicollinearity. I have attached the output.
> >
> >
> > I have also attempted the regression this way around:
> >
> > F1 + F2 + F3 ~ LONELINESS
> >
> > but this time there were standardised estimates greater than 1 between F1 and LONELINESS.
> >
> > Would you have any suggestions for addressing these sign reversals or perhaps suggestions for how to specify this model?
> >
> > Thank you,
> > Ellen
> >
> --

All,

I am running GenomicSEM GWAS and am getting the following error for certain SNPs.

Error in eigen(V_Full) : infinite or missing values in 'x'

This seems not to occur genome-wide (running for about 3 million SNPs), although whenever it occurs it kills the GenomicSEM GWAS run. Is there a way that I can try and catch such an error and have the model run for other SNPs?

Thank You,
Ravi
